assertions.evidence: Paragraphs 1–2 give the orientation and order: “west start → north alcove → pick up lantern → return through the 1.4 m path → use pedestal → pass gate.” The pedestal is beside the east gate.
Paragraph 2 says “The south pinch fails the 1.2 m carrying minimum.” Paragraph 3 specifies dragging the 1.2 m template through the route and observing the gate in a paper walkthrough.
Paragraph 1 starts “before the first junction with the east-facing camera” with fresh participants and records “first cue noticed, first junction choice” before the 30-second help point.
Paragraph 1 says “Earlier supported runs establish reachability only.” Paragraph 2 compares the current view with a view framing the north landmark while holding the marker constant.
Paragraph 1 derives the result from “min(15, 3 + 3n)” and the balances 3, 6, 9 and 12. The baseline unlock is match 3 and the proposal is match 2.
Paragraph 2 leaves the decision with the progression owner and says “Stop adoption if a player can acquire or use the unlock before the required tutorial step,” including exactly 9 coins.

Paragraphs 1–2 start from save revision 3 at 80 coins. Grandfathering leaves “80 usable coins after migration and reload.” Truncation yields “one recorded change from 80 to 60 and unchanged 60 on replay.”
Paragraph 3 keeps the treatment of the 20 excess coins with the owner. Paragraph 2 names additional loss on replay, an over-cap grant and resurrected coins as direct falsifiers.
Paragraph 1 records “input 72, confirmation 90, sound 155, recovery 430” and calculates the margins separately, including input 28 ms before cutoff.

Paragraph 2 holds build, device, cue, cutoff, recovery and input fixed and changes sound timing. Paragraph 1 says delayed acknowledgement and window uncertainty “are both plausible,” consistent with one trace.

Paragraph 1 distinguishes paused queue leakage from a fresh resume-edge input in the ordinary active-time handler. Paragraph 2 requests active and wall timestamps and native queue writes and reads, preserving the observed ambiguity.

Paragraph 2 runs an unpaused equivalent active tick, paused press-and-release with untouched resume, then resume-edge press with no paused action. It assigns different observations to a pre-resume enqueue and a new post-resume edge.

Paragraph 1 requires voluntary consent and recording approval. Paragraph 2 gives fresh participants the same visible item and state, uses “Get your character ready to use the item shown,” and forbids pointing, naming controls or demonstrating before first observation.
Paragraphs 2–3 record the first uncoached action, close unaided observation at a time limit, opt-out or help request, and put explicitly eligible counts and icon selection before the design owner.
Paragraph 1 gives “Baseline: 4/8 correct” and “Candidate: 5/7 correct,” explicitly excluding the two and four coached rehearsals and the one candidate without an opportunity.

Paragraph 1 leaves the cue effect unresolved because of sample size, nonrandom assignment, build differences and mixed devices. Paragraph 2 proposes same build and entry with cue-only variation and matching or randomization by device.
Paragraph 1 names “pattern-overwatch@1, evidence trace-O.” Paragraph 2 separately identifies “pattern-warning-cone@2, evidence trace-W” as display-only.
The tactical corridor allows facing and arming during the active tactical turn and an enemy-movement reaction. The always-visible tutorial preview is unsuitable where it cannot arm or react.
Paragraph 1 names pattern-windup@3 and pattern-resource-charge@1 and distinguishes a held input that resolves on release from a stored use granted at refill.

Paragraph 2 checks hold lengths and effective release in the tutorial versus one refill and one eligible spend at the shop. It closes with “Both links remain conditional” pending exact source/build pins and owner confirmation.
